Filed by architect-16a01670 2026-09-04, measured at main 9e9b7b04. WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the one shell-wide pause fact (poll + React context) and the status-strip banner. NO Seats panel, board next-step, e2e or runbook (3c, 3d). MEASURED (re-measure before planning): - apps/control-room/src/v2/cordum-app.tsx (388 lines, pre-existing over cap - minimal edit, record the size): the attached session is `attached` (:148; headers at `attached.headers`), the shell renders at :368-386 ``; the Health screen's own poll (v2/ops/live-ops.tsx `useOpsRead` :28-60, POLL_MS 5000) mounts ONLY on the health view (:323-324), so no pause fact exists shell-wide today. - apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/cordum-shell.tsx (195): renders `` at :183; status-strip.tsx (152): `cr.shell.statusstrip` :75, the connection chip :98, `cr.shell.stale` :99-101; status-strip.test.tsx (156). - Context pattern to copy: v2/shell/proof-context.tsx (createContext + frozen NO_OP fallback + Provider + hook). - `readHealth(headers)` = apps/control-room/src/live/live-ops.ts:273; the paused shape is 3a's `HealthOutcome["agents"]["paused"]`. FEATURE: new apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/pause-context.tsx exporting `ProviderPause` (alias of 3a's paused object type), `ProviderPauseProvider({ value, children })` and `useProviderPause(): ProviderPause | null` (null with no provider - fail-safe, a unit-rendered screen never crashes). cordum-app.tsx polls `readHealth(attached.headers)` every 15 s while attached (same generation/inFlight discipline as useOpsRead; stops on detach; a REFUSED/ERROR answer keeps the last known pause for one poll then clears it) and wraps the shell tree in the provider; `CordumShell` gains `paused?: ProviderPause | null` and passes it to `StatusStrip`, which renders `Agents paused: limit, resumes ` between the connection chip and the stale marker while paused, and nothing otherwise.
definitionOfDone: status-strip.test.tsx arms: with `paused` the strip renders cr.shell.paused with the exact sentence 'Agents paused: claude limit, resumes <time>' (the time computed in the test from the same resetAt with the same locale call), without it `queryByTestId('cr.shell.paused')` is null; the existing strip arms stay green unchanged (count line quoted).
pause-context test: `useProviderPause()` returns null with no provider and the provided value with one; the provider re-renders consumers when the value changes.

cordum-app.tsx polls readHealth with the attached headers every 15 s and only while attached (a test with an injected reader if cordum-app has a test file - grep `cordum-app.test`; otherwise a cordum-shell.test arm proving a `paused` prop reaches the strip plus a source-text pin that cordum-app renders `<ProviderPauseProvider`), and the shell shows the banner on EVERY view (goals, board, needs-you, runs, policy, health).

Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`; pause-context.tsx, status-strip.tsx, cordum-shell.tsx stay <= 250 (`wc -l` quoted), cordum-app.tsx growth <= 25 lines over its pre-existing 388; sources ASCII-only, JSX text apostrophe-free; every arm mutated red once.
taskRails: ONE POLL: the shell-wide pause fact is read once per app, never once per screen; consumers read the context.
FAIL-SAFE CONTEXT: a screen rendered without the provider sees null and renders no banner - never a crash, never a fabricated pause.
NO Seats/board/e2e/docs change (3c, 3d); <=250 lines per production source except the pre-existing cordum-app.tsx; ASCII-only sources; JSX apostrophe-free.

Surface, verbatim:
- `export type ProviderPause = ProviderPauseView` - a type-only re-export of 3a's own decoded shape, imported `import type { ProviderPauseView } from "../../live/live-ops.js";`. Deliberately the control-room twin, NOT apps/daemon's identically-named interface: @moe/control-room has no @moe/daemon dependency, the repo has no tsconfig "paths" and no project references, so a deep relative import to the daemon is a TS6059 build break (gotcha-health-read-agents-pause-decoder-twins item 4). Alias, not a redeclaration, so the strip can never drift from the decoder.
- `const PauseContext = createContext<ProviderPause | null>(null)` - module-private. The fallback is `null` itself rather than proof-context's frozen NO_OP object, because the absence of a provider and the absence of a pause are the same statement here ("nothing known"), and a sentinel object would have to be distinguished by every consumer.
- `export function ProviderPauseProvider(props: { readonly children: ReactNode; readonly value: ProviderPause | null }): JSX.Element`
- `export function useProviderPause(): ProviderPause | null`

Four arms, all green: (1) `<Consumer />` with NO provider renders "NONE" - the fail-safe rail, an unwrapped screen never crashes; (2) inside `<ProviderPauseProvider value={PAUSE}>` the probe reads `claude|2026-09-02T20:30:00.000Z|node.deliver@node-1` (provider + resetAt + workItemId, so a partial read cannot pass); (3) `rerender` with a different value updates the consumer (claude -> codex, resetAt follows) AND then with `value={null}` drops back to "NONE" - that second half is the pause-CLEARING edge, which is the one the next poll actually exercises; (4) `value={null}` on first render reads "NONE".

The PAUSE literal is 3a's own fixture copied verbatim from apps/control-room/src/live/live-ops.test.ts:20-24 (including `lastLine: "You've hit your weekly limit - resets Sep 8, 10:46am (Asia/Jerusalem)"`), so the context arm and the decoder arm describe one pause, not two invented ones. From child 3a (task-278faf81c10845ffa571716105aa19e3), landed on moe/work-2026-09-04. What you consume, measured, not designed:

TYPE TO IMPORT: `ProviderPauseView` from `apps/control-room/src/live/live-ops.ts` (a TYPE-only export; `import type { ProviderPauseView } from "../../live/live-ops.js"` - adjust depth). Do NOT import the daemon's identically-named `ProviderPauseView` from apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts: @moe/control-room has no dependency on @moe/daemon (deps = contracts, control-room-client, control-room-model, core), the repo has no tsconfig "paths" and no project references, so a deep relative import fails TS6059. The two declarations are deliberate twins kept in step by the exact-key decoder.

FIELD TO READ: `outcome.agents.paused` on the HEALTH arm of `HealthOutcome`, i.e.
  readonly agents: { readonly paused: ProviderPauseView | null }
`ProviderPauseView = { lastLine: string; provider: string; resetAt: string; since: string; workItemId: string }` - all five REQUIRED, all string, none nullable. `paused === null` means no provider is paused. Reach it only inside the `outcome.status === "HEALTH"` narrowing.

FOUR THINGS THAT WILL BITE YOUR BANNER:
1. `lastLine` MAY BE THE EMPTY STRING. A pause whose cause never named a line is a REAL pause (the daemon maps a null cause/lastLine to ""), so do not treat "" as absent and do not render an empty quote. There is an arm on this in live-ops.test.ts.
2. `lastLine` IS NOT LENGTH-BOUNDED IN THE BROWSER. The daemon clips at 512 chars (child 1's LAST_LINE_MAX_CHARS) but `pausedOf` only checks `typeof === "string"`. If you render it, clamp/truncate it yourself - it is a provider-authored line arriving over the wire.
3. `resetAt` IS ONLY CHECKED NON-EMPTY, NOT ISO. `new Date(resetAt)` can be Invalid Date. HealthScreen's `agentsWords` (ops-screens.tsx) handles this by `Date.parse` + `Number.isNaN(at) ? paused.resetAt : new Date(at).toLocaleString()` - show the raw instant, never "Invalid Date", and never hide the pause behind a formatting miss. Copy that shape; there is an arm pinning it.
4. ONE PROVIDER AT A TIME. The daemon reports the FIRST live pause in `KNOWN_PROVIDERS` order (`["claude","codex"]`, exported from apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts). Two providers paused -> claude is reported and codex is invisible until claude clears. Deliberate, since one banner is rendered - do not write a DoD clause expecting both.

ALREADY TAKEN, DO NOT RE-IMPLEMENT: the `cr.health.agents` testid (a Fact labelled "Agents" inside `cr.health.facts`, reading "not paused" or "paused: <provider> limit, resumes <resetAt in the reader's locale>"), the exact-key decoder roster `["agents","daemon","ledger","outcome","readAt","verifier"]`, and every HEALTH fixture in live-ops.test.ts and ops-screens.test.tsx (both already carry `agents: { paused: null }`; a fixture you add without it will not typecheck).

FAIL-CLOSED CONTRACT you inherit: a frame with no `agents`, an extra key inside `agents`, an extra or missing key inside `paused`, or a non-string field is OPS_RESPONSE_INVALID at CONTROL_ROOM_LIVE_OPS. `paused: null` is accepted. Seven drift arms pin this; if you widen the shape, widen those arms in the same row.
